coverage.main: Read all fifteen pages of arXiv 2002.05990v1 (ICLR 2020 camera-ready header), including Sections 1-5, Tables 1-7, Figures 1-4, references and Appendices A-C (Tables 8-11, Figures 5-6).
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-C are embedded in the arXiv PDF and were read. The paper links no separate supplement or code; the authors' later repository (released 18 November 2020 with the 5,000-image subset) was located by search and inspected as an artifact, not as paper text.
coverage.excluded_results: Figure 4 (white-box FGSM/SGM strength and epsilon sweep) and same-architecture diagonal cells (RN152->RN152, DN201->DN201, and ensemble members RN152/DN201 in Table 6) are white-box and excluded from transfer judgments. Appendix Tables 8-9 rows for other papers summarize prior work; only the 'Ours' rows are retained as setup evidence. Figure 5 is visual.

result_groups.locator: Section 3.3 and Table 1 (p. 5); Section 4 Threat Model (p. 6); Tables 2-4 and Figure 2 (pp. 6-8); Table 6 (p. 9); Appendix Tables 8-9 'Ours' unsecured columns (pp. 14-15)
result_groups.population: 5,000 random ImageNet validation images correctly classified by all eight source models; five random seeds
result_groups.outcome: untargeted black-box success rate (mean +/- std over 5 runs)
result_groups.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 4 filter images correct on all source models. That covers target clean correctness only when the target is itself one of the eight sources (RN152, DN201); VGG19, SE154, IncV3, IncV4 and IncResV2 are not covered, and source-only filtering is not evidence that target-clean errors were excluded. Success rate is not defined with respect to source success. The released evaluator computes top-1 accuracy over all saved adversarial images (README: success = 1 - acc), which retains source failures operationally, but correspondence to every table is not established.

result_groups.locator: Section 4.2 and Table 5 (p. 8); Table 7 (p. 9); Appendix Tables 8-9 'Ours' secured columns including appendix-only DI+SGM values
result_groups.population: Same source-filtered 5,000-image set; 20-step attacks against three ensemble-adversarially-trained Inception targets
result_groups.outcome: untargeted black-box success rate (mean +/- std over 5 runs)
result_groups.evidence: Same source-only filter; secured targets are never sources. No clean accuracy or target-clean filter stated; success-rate denominator not defined relative to source success.

result_groups.population: 5,000 ImageNet validation images; Figure 1 and Figure 3 captions/text describe random validation images without restating the correct-classification filter
result_groups.evidence: Graphical ablations (Figure 1 prints two rates, 52.52% and 62.10%, for ResNet-18 -> VGG19). No clean-correct or source-success conditioning is stated for these panels.

f1.evidence: No clean accuracy is reported for sources or targets (only an SE154 top-5 error remark). The source filter implies 100% source accuracy on the cohort by construction, which is not a reported clean accuracy. Missing values are not an explicit pooled report.

f2.evidence: All groups unclear: the 'correctly classified by all source models' wording covers only targets that are also sources. Preserve this partial positive filtering evidence for RN152/DN201 targets; any_explicit_yes = false at group level.

f3.evidence: Success rate is not defined relative to source success in the paper. Released evaluator behaviour (all adversarial images scored) is recorded as artifact evidence, not substituted for a reporting judgment.

f4.evidence: Nominal denominator 5,000 is stated, but most rates are means over five random runs, so per-run integer numerators are not uniquely recoverable; figure values are graphical. Appendix Table 8 'Ours FGSM' values duplicate the PGD row (26.56/21.03/19.10) and differ from Table 2 FGSM values, and several prose values (35.48%, 65.38%, 80.52%) differ slightly from the tables; recorded as reporting inconsistencies, not error claims.

f5.locator: Figure 1 caption (p. 2); Section 3.3 (p. 5); Section 4 Threat Model (p. 6); Appendix Table 11 (p. 15)
f5.evidence: Untargeted attacks under maximum L-infinity epsilon 16 on [0,255] pixels 'for all attack methods', including the case study, ensemble and secured experiments; Table 11 restates epsilon 16. Figure 3's ablation does not restate epsilon but falls under the stated all-methods threat model.

f6.locator: Appendix B (p. 14) model sources; artifact_checks below
f6.evidence: The paper links no code. The authors' later repository provides attack and evaluation scripts, a Google Drive/Baidu 5,000-image subset and uses public pretrainedmodels/torchvision weights (the paper's stated model sources). The Drive page and two torchvision weight files respond, but data contents, checkpoint identity and execution were not verified. Released attack step size epsilon/steps (1.6 for 10 steps) differs from the stated alpha = 2; README command labels also swap source architectures. Recorded as a recomputation candidate, not yes.

artifact_checks.result: Cloned and pinned. attack_sgm.py (advertorch PGD/MI with SGM hooks, default epsilon 16/255, step epsilon/num_steps, clip [0,1]) and evaluate.py (top-1 accuracy over all images in the adversarial folder against ground truth). README reports its own reproduced RN152/DN201 -> VGG19 values (e.g., SGM 81.04% vs paper 79.90%). Not executed.
HTTP HEAD 200 on the Drive viewer page; archive not downloaded, so image identity and count are unverified.

HTTP HEAD 200 (81,131,730 bytes); resnet152-b121ed2d.pth also 200 (241,530,880 bytes). The pretrainedmodels mirror data.lip6.fr failed TLS through the review tool. Weights not downloaded; identity with the paper's checkpoints not established.

bounds_checks.reason: No target clean accuracy on the source-filtered 5,000-image cohort is reported; full-ImageNet benchmark accuracies must not be substituted. Rates are also multi-run means. Not eligible without recomputation.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Operational evaluator evidence and the paper/code step-size difference are recorded for recomputation planning, not as findings about the published tables.
No download of the data archive or weights, and no execution.
